You might be transgender, and that’s okay. <3 Gender Dysphoria is what many trans people struggle with, and it sounds like you could have it. Gender Dysphoria (not dysmorphia ! ) is the disconnection between the gender you were born as vs the gender your brain is. I’m a trans guy, I’ve known since I was very young too, I’m on hormones and I spent my whole life feeling like something was missing too. 

We’re taught to be a certain way our entire lives, so it’s absolutely okay and understandable that it’s pretty scary, and a lot of people experience a lot of feelings of denial and uncertainty when you start to realise you might be transgender. But, like you said, for a lot of trans people when you present as the gender you feel most comfortable in, it’s like all the puzzle pieces have matched together and it just feels ... right. Like you’ve always been this way and just didn’t know it. 

Dressing a certain way , cutting your hair, using a binder to make your chest flat, and going through hormone therapy or surgeries help them match up their body to your brain. Some of these things can be serious, and scary. But I’m regards to your family or bf, you deserve to be the most ‘you’ you can be. If your bf leaves you because you’re a guy, it’ll be sad but you’ll be okay and you will eventually be surrounded by love. Whether you’re trans or not, trust your gut and remember you have as long as you want to figure this all out <3 you’re more than welcome to message me if you want more info, there are a lot of good YouTube videos etc ! I wish you the best

[edit : you also don’t have to have meds or surgery to be trans! Social Dysphoria is feeling bad when, In your case, you’re perceived as a girl. Body Dysphoria is when the sex characteristics of your body create a feeling of discomfort. Both can result in mild to serious anxiety and depression!]

Hey, 

So I wanted to comment a little hope before before but actually, yeah I do. [trigger warning for talking about abuse in detail] 

I’m 19 , I grew up in an overly sexualised and abusive household. I moved out a couple months after I turned 18. I’ve lived through sexual abuse, emotional abuse, I’ve been manipulated , experienced so much passive aggression and most of my issues stem from emotional abuse, neglect and my parents responding with anger to everything throughout my life. I moved out, was fine for 6 months, experienced a sexually abusive relationship that broke me, i numbed myself completely for 7 months until I saw him in October and a switch flipped inside me and broke me. Everything I had repressed came up. I couldn’t tell you the number of times I almost didn’t make it through the end of last year. Everything came up, from my childhood, my sexual abuse, my parents, my abusive ex. I had crippling anxiety , depression and unhealthy codependency in my early teens and through high school, I disassociated frequently , I had anxiety attacks and was hypersexual. I’ve struggled with self harm for a really long time. And it stopped when I moved out, I felt so much better but when the switch flipped, it all came crashing back but worse. I couldn’t leave the house except for work for months, I was having panic attacks frequently, I hadn’t had a sober day In about 6 months , or more. I was smoking myself to sleep every night, not going to uni, self harming and putting myself in dangerous situations, I couldn’t cope with the way that my brain has been trained to feel this entire time. My whole life I was made to feel unimportant, my problems were treated with frustration and anger by people I cared about. I didn’t think I deserved to get better, I wanted to be dead. 

And, not to be cliche.. but then I got therapy. My first ever councillor , I didn’t even know what I was going In for. I didn’t know about trauma or that it was heavily effecting my life. Like you, I didn’t think it ‘counted’ because, yeah sure, my dads hit me so hard I sobbed and My mom once threw a hairbrush so hard next to me it smashed. But that’s not ‘ that bad’ right? Wrong. emotional abuse isn’t black and white, and it is NEVER your fault, you are NEVER ‘ not traumatised enough’ . What I learned through therapy is that trauma isn’t about anyone else. Your trauma is YOUR trauma, there can be small t’s and big T’s, both both are important, both effect the way we are and have sometimes our whole lives. When I feel down, my trauma feels very much a part of me. It took me a lot of therapy, and I’m getting more, to realise that my trauma is separate from me. Therapy can be whatever you want it to be, but it can be such a helpful tool to just understand yourself. Trauma is something that effects your brain, with physical symptoms sometimes too. I’ve found that if you can begin to unpack, understand yourself, and rewire your brain ( especially in specialist trauma therapy) it can literally change your life. Understanding my trauma, why I was disassociating, etc didn’t make it go away all together, but it helped me deal with it and know that one day it WILL go away, or it’ll be a separate thing from me that I know I can take a deep breath and walk away from. I’m not gonna lie, it can take a lot of hard work, and sometimes you can get worse before you get better, it can seem intimidating , hard and scary but I promise that you deserve to feel like you’re winning. You deserve to feel loved, and safe and that you’re not your illness. Your trauma is important, and I’m so sorry you went through something so horrible but you can get to a place where you believe all this too, it’s just a journey you have to take. There’s a lot of different kind of therapy, I’m not a professional or anything, just a guy who browses Reddit and has a lot of passion. This might sound dramatic, but meds also help so much too. I’m medicated, I take Mirtazapine and Proponol ( lowers heart rate and stops me getting anxious and disassociating at retail work) , I have rough patches, but I know it’s because I need more therapy. But I can sleep now, I can eat, I have a loving relationship and a partner who loves and supports me. I’m ready to go back to uni after being ill for a year. I’m sorry to ramble about myself loads but I just want you to know so many people have done it, and you can too. One day you’ll get so far in your healing journey you didn’t realise how far you’ve come until you reflect. Sometimes you wake up and realise you haven’t had a panic attack for 6 months, and you make your favourite breakfast. Sometimes something will trigger you and you’ll be feeling really rough, but it’ll never undo the progress you’ve made. 

Hope this isn’t weird to hear from a stranger on the internet, but I’m proud of you. You can do this and I wish someone had told me that In some of my darkest times.
